title: How stable is Eshelby uniformity to shape imperfections?
summary: If a real inclusion departs from the ellipsoid family by a measured amount, how much interior strain heterogeneity must appear, and which geometric scales control the error?

statement.lead: Let q(Ω) measure whole-interior strain heterogeneity and let ρ(Ω,𝓔) measure distance from the ellipsoid family after removing exact ellipsoidal degrees of freedom. The quantitative stability target is
statement.after: The upper bound asks whether nearly ellipsoidal shapes are nearly uniform; the lower bound asks whether nearly uniform interior fields force the shape to be near some ellipsoid. The appropriate shape metric is part of the mechanics because morphological wavelength matters.

why: Eshelby's ellipsoidal inclusion solution is foundational to micromechanics, but real precipitates, transforming regions, and engineered inclusions are not exact ellipsoids.
A quantitative stability theory turns an ellipsoidal approximation from a geometric convenience into a controlled mechanical approximation with an explicit error estimate.
The problem also exposes which geometric information must be retained: equal-amplitude shape errors at different wavelengths need not produce equal elastic heterogeneity.
scope: Results in the 2026 preprint assume an infinite three-dimensional homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic solid, uniform dilatational eigenstrain, identical inclusion and matrix moduli, perfect bonding, and no remote loading.

The nonlinear geometry-only two-sided theorem applies in a sufficiently small smooth neighborhood of any fixed nondegenerate ellipsoid. A separate residual-field construction gives convergent bounds for a prescribed bounded finite geometry and does not require that local neighborhood.
The local shape distance is measured relative to the nearby ellipsoid family rather than one arbitrarily chosen reference ellipsoid.

Open extensions include a global geometry-only two-sided stability law, general eigenstrain modes, elastic contrast, anisotropy, free surfaces and interfaces, periodic domains, and multiple interacting inclusions.

boundary.text: Eshelby established exact uniform interior strain for ellipsoidal inclusions in the classical setting.

Local and inverse results show that the ellipsoid family is the natural exact-uniformity set: Markenscoff identified its local tangent structure, and the weak three-dimensional Eshelby conjecture was subsequently proved.

Perturbative fields for weakly non-spherical inclusions and constrained progress on the strong conjecture quantify important nearby and inverse regimes, but they do not supply the full two-sided stability law posed here.
Recent multiphysical inclusion work extends exact field/uniformity theory but does not close the quantitative near-ellipsoid stability problem.

Ni (2026, arXiv preprint) proves nonlinear two-sided local control of whole-interior strain heterogeneity by a geometry-only distance to the nearby ellipsoid family, after removing changes that produce another ellipsoid, in the stated homogeneous-isotropic dilatational setting.

The half-order Sobolev scale is the critical order for frequency-independent two-sided control. The preprint derives the exact linear spectrum and sharp all-mode bounds for a sphere after removing its ellipsoidal directions.

For prescribed finite geometries in the same physical setting, ellipsoidal subtraction gives an exact residual-field budget and lower and upper bounds from partial interior and exterior field information. With exact integration, the bounds converge to the exact heterogeneity as the resolved regions exhaust the respective domains.

Numerical evidence: the preprint applies the finite-shape bounds to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions and compares them with independently assembled displacement-based finite-element calculations.

The convergent construction for a specified finite geometry is distinct from a global two-sided law in terms of geometry-only distance to ellipsoids. Such a global law, and extensions to general eigenstrains, elastic mismatch, anisotropy, boundaries, periodicity and interacting inclusions, remain open.

settle: Prove a geometry-only two-sided stability relation beyond the local neighborhood, or extend the relation to a more general eigenstrain, material or boundary setting, with the shape class and norm stated precisely.
A sharp counterexample showing that a proposed global metric or stability statement cannot hold would materially settle part of the problem.
Obtain effective local constants for general nonspherical ellipsoids, including their dependence on aspect ratio and the admissible neighborhood.
Extend computable geometry-to-field error bounds and independent validation to additional material, loading or boundary settings relevant to real inclusions.

progress.title: Preprint available: local stability and convergent finite-shape bounds
progress.text: The arXiv preprint reports nonlinear two-sided local stability, the critical half-order geometric scale with an exact sphere spectrum, and convergent bounds for prescribed finite geometries. Independent displacement-based finite-element comparisons provide numerical evidence. EL01 now distinguishes these results from the remaining global geometry-only and broader physical-setting questions.

progress.title: Local nonlinear two-sided stability assembled
progress.text: The current study develops a manuscript-stage local theorem around general nondegenerate ellipsoids in the homogeneous-isotropic dilatational setting.

progress.title: Finite-shape enclosure and independent FEM comparison
progress.text: A complementary shape-specific residual-field enclosure was paired with an independently assembled displacement-based elasticity calculation.
